Hannah / Daniel — thanks for the 30-minute sync earlier. Quick written recap so we have the same assumptions and clear next steps.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary workload: real-time clinical summarization + patient-facing chat (high token churn on short prompts).
- Expected steady-state avg tokens / month: 90M–150M (you said current pilot averages ~120M).
- SLA requirement: EU data residency for PHI-adjacent logs; low single-token latency for chat critical flows.
- Budget frame you shared (directional): $90k–$180k / month (you asked for target $/1M tokens to compare).

Immediate asks I promised to follow up on:
1) Baseline unit economics: ballpark $/1M tokens for Hosted (US) and hosted (EU) tiers + delta for Dedicated reserved capacity.
2) Clarify the residency surcharge we apply when storing logs and telemetry in EU-only clusters.
3) Attach a lightweight pricing worksheet (attached) so you can plug in your exact volumes.

Attachments: Lumen-Pricing-Worksheet.xlsx (worksheet), Redwood-EU-Hosting-SLA.pdf (SLA/residency notes).

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send a detailed unit-econ note in about 45 minutes with line-item math.
- If the numbers look sensible, propose a 30-min procurement + security sync next week to discuss SOC2 evidence and contract cadence.

Thanks — Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- EU residency: we need all logs and PKI-stored artifacts to remain in EU for patients in the EU; for US patients we can use US. Is that something Redwood can support at the customer-account level?
- Budget: the $90k–$180k / month is the leadership range; target for procurement is to hit < $1,000 per 1M tokens ideally (we know this varies by latency tier).
- Volumes: pilot months have spiky peaks up to ~220M tokens; sustained estimate for Q4 is ~120M.

If you can show the per-1M token delta between US hosted and EU-hosted (and where Dedicated makes sense), that will help the procurement team decide between Hosted + residency addon vs Dedicated EU pool.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (pricing assumptions)

Hannah — appreciate the clarity. Below is the concise unit-econ breakdown (ballpark, list-price before any committed discounts). I kept scenarios simple so you can map to the worksheet.

Assumptions (for the math below):
- "1M tokens" shorthand is 1,000,000 tokens processed (generation + input).
- Hosted = Redwood managed multi-tenant serving (fastest onboarding).
- Dedicated = reserved GPU pools (lower unit price at scale, contract required).
- Residency addon = storing logs/trace/telemetry in EU-only region and routing all EU traffic to EU cluster.

Ballpark list prices (per 1M tokens):
- Hosted (US region): $820 / 1M tokens
- Hosted (EU region): $975 / 1M tokens (≈ +19% regional delta driven by EU capacity footprint and vault/KMS costs)
- Dedicated (EU reserved pool, committed 12mo, >100M/mo): $590 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated (US reserved pool, committed 12mo, >100M/mo): $520 / 1M tokens
- Residency addon (account-level EU-only logging + HSM keys): flat surcharge = $0.00 per 1M tokens on top of region price but requires Dedicated EU or Hosted EU with monthly service premium; operational uplift is reflected in the region delta above.

Example monthly scenarios (approx):
1) Pilot peak month (220M tokens) — Hosted EU: 220 * $975 = $214,500 / mo (list)
2) Sustained Q4 (120M tokens) — Hosted US: 120 * $820 = $98,400 / mo (list)
3) Sustained Q4 w/ Dedicated EU (>100M commit): 120 * $590 = $70,800 / mo (list)

Interpretation / guidance:
- Your stated procurement target (< $1,000 / 1M tokens) is compatible with Hosted US (list $820) but EU-hosted list exceeds that — EU delta is the main driver.
- If EU data residency is mandatory for EU traffic, the cleanest unit-econ path at your volume is Dedicated EU reserved capacity — it lowers per-token cost and gives capacity isolation for PHI-adjacent flows.
- Hosted EU is simplest but ~19% more expensive; for sporadic EU traffic this can be fine. For sustained EU token volumes >50–70M/month, Dedicated EU often becomes the more economical route after you factor in discounts/commits.

Open items I’ll need to finalize a firm quote:
- Callouts in your security questionnaire re: EU HSM / KMS provider (we support common KMS vendors; need vendor preference).
- Exact expected split of EU vs US tokens per month (even a 3-point estimate helps).
- Commitment horizon you’d be comfortable with (3/12/24 months) — larger terms get steeper discounts.

I’ve updated the attached worksheet with the above list prices so you can model scenarios. If useful, I can run 2 quick SKU quotes (Hosted EU vs Dedicated EU 12mo) and share a short comparison doc.

Next suggested calendar steps:
- Procurement + Security sync (30 min) — propose Tue 2026-09-21 09:00 PT / 18:00 CET — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.
- If procurement wants committed pricing, we’ll scope the Dedicated sizing and present a draft term sheet.

Thanks — Marcus
